doc.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]

chapter: New York studio and TV work
title: Early rock and roll sessions with jazz guitarists
summary: He played on Dion and the Belmonts records alongside Mundell Lowe, George Barnes and others, and discusses the swing feel in early rock.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Just that little lick that you were singing reminds me of a Paul Anka song. You did those things. © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-
Oh yeah, we made a lot of those. I made all records. The first six records with Dion and the Belmonts I had Mundell Lowe was on guitar, George Barnes, all jazz guys on those rock & roll records.

Yeah. Billy Bauer from the Woody Herman band, Osie Johnson, Panama Francis played drums, and none of us had those exotic guitars they use, that you see on these videos today. We had old fashioned archtop guitars with little Diamond pick-ups on them.
It’s interesting when you listen to some of the early — especially the Chuck Berry records — that he was into the straight eighth note rock & roll thing.
But the rhythm section was kind of still playing a swing mode.
Like they’re feeling each other, like what’s going on here now.
